newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower on light volumes.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower on light volumes.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended lower Tuesday, despite rumors of central bank activity, with the volume in COMEX copper exceeding the volume in COMEX gold.
"There was very little of note going on in precious metals today, other than some rolling of May silver positions into the July contract," FIMAT New York trader John Tyree said.
COMEX June gold settled down $1.50 an ounce at $343.40, after trading a $345.10-342.90 range. Estimated total COMEX gold volume was only 11,000 lots.
Bullion banks were the main sellers, rather than the funds, traders said, amid rumors of unconfirmed rumors of European central bank activity, traders said.
But the Dutch central bank denied it had been selling gold. In January this year the Dutch central bank confirmed it had sold 300 tonnes of its gold reserves in late 1996.

Daily momentum oscillators in June gold, such as a standard nine-day relative strength indicator (RSI), have recovered from the oversold levels seen after last week's slump to contract lows, but the momentum downtrend had not yet reversed, analysts said.
Meanwhile, the contract's five-day moving average remained well below both its 21-day and 55-day average, suggesting the renewed downtrend was still intact.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $341.10/60 compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $341.60 and the New York close Monday around $342.70/10.

While physical offtake is seen robust below $340 an ounce, concerns about the possibility of another rise in U.S. interest rates at the next Federal Reserve FOMC meeting on May 20, as well as worries about further European central bank activity are likely to limit any advance in gold, analysts said.

In producer news, South Africa's Free State Consolidated Gold Mines Ltd Freegold said Tuesday a fire at its Western Holdings No 1 shaft had hit about six kilograms of production and there could be further losses.
Meanwhile, workers went on strike at South Africa's East Rand Propietary Mines Ltd.
COMEX May silver ended down 2.0 cents at $4.715, after seeing a $4.770-4.705 range. Estimated total COMEX silver volume was 21,000 contracts.
Open interest in COMEX silver fell a sharp 2,130 lots Monday to 99,266 contracts, after climbing to its highest levels since August last year on Friday at 102,323 contracts.
Silver prices have also changed little in the past few days, after finding support around $4.70 in the bullion market last week, following a slide to two-month lows.

Fundamentals in silver are more bullish than for gold, analysts said. Despite rising mine production since 1995, consumption is expected to reach record levels in the U.S. and India this year, while COMEX stocks have declined by nearly 50 percent since 1994.
NYMEX July platinum ended down $4.10 an ounce at $376.40, while NYMEX June palladium lost $1.00 to $154.75, on light profit taking, but the physical market remained very tight, traders said.
PGM lease rates remained high in Zurich, traders said, with the physical market likely to stay very tight until Russian supplies to Japan resume.
The fundamental outlook for PGMs remains the most bullish of any metals in the precious metals complex, analysts said.

Heavy supplies of platinum and palladium from Russia last year swamped the market, but Russian PGM exports have fallen sharply this year after the breakdown of the Russia/Japan supplycontract talks in December.
The large supply/demand surpluses of the past three or four years are now being absorbed and automotive demand is rising quickly, analysts said.
